problem_definition.requested_solution: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds
symptoms: Customers wait forever; a chatbot would answer instantly.
problem_definition.root_problem: IBAN format errors in refund payment data cause failed refunds, which leads customers to inquire about refund status, perceived as long wait times.

trace.summary: IBAN format errors in refund payment data cause failed refunds, which leads customers to inquire about refund status, perceived as long wait times.

details.requested_solution: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds

structural_remedies.description: Implement IBAN format validation and cleansing at payment intake and in existing refund payment data to prevent FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT errors (E-01, A-ASSUMPTION-1, A-ASSUMPTION-2).
structural_remedies.rationale: Data quality improvements can be done via scripts and validation rules within the remaining 150 minutes.; residual gap: Some inquiries may persist from other issue types or perception (U-UNKNOWN-1, U-UNKNOWN-3). Still need to verify impact on inquiry volume (VOB-U-UNKNOWN-1).

structural_remedies.description: Deploy a self‑service refund status lookup (portal/IVR) so customers can check refund status without contacting support (E-03, CL-02).
structural_remedies.rationale: A simple status lookup can be built using existing ticket and payment data within remaining time.; residual gap: If IBAN errors are not fully resolved, some failures will still generate inquiries; self‑service addresses the perception gap (U-UNKNOWN-2).

solution_design.bridge_sunset_condition: When VOB-U-UNKNOWN-1 is resolved (i.e., improving IBAN data quality is verified to reduce refund failures enough to lower inquiries) and the IBAN validation remedy (SR-01) is deployed.
unfinished_scope: known limitation: Maintain median response time for refund inquiries under the 2‑hour SLA.

current_plan.rationale: Execute read-only queries to obtain current refund failure counts (E-01) and ticket response times (E-02) needed to design a self‑service refund status tool that addresses stakeholder‑perceived wait times (E-03). This grounds the solution in observed data rather than assumptions alone. (E-01, E-02, E-03). The queries are read‑only, so they produce no side effects and are inherently reversible. Alternatives would be to skip data collection and rely solely on stakeholder input and assumptions, but that would increase risk of mis‑aligned solution. (R-11)

framing_assertion.rationale: The request asserts that customers are waiting too long for answers about refunds.

hypotheses.statement: Customers experience long wait times for refund-related inquiries due to insufficient support capacity.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, a chatbot that handles refund queries would directly reduce wait times.

hypotheses.statement: Customers lack accessible self-service information about refund process, leading them to contact support.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, improving knowledge base or FAQ would reduce contacts more than a chatbot alone.

hypotheses.statement: Refund payment processing is delayed, causing customers to inquire about status via support.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, expediting payment processing would reduce status-check tickets.

hypotheses.statement: Refund-related tickets are misrouted or stuck in queues due to poor ticket assignment rules.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, fixing routing rules would cut wait times without a chatbot.

proposal.summary: IBAN format errors in refund payment data cause failed refunds (E-01), leading customers to inquire about refund status, which is perceived as long wait times (E-03). The problem was established by evidence of refund failures (E-01), median response time within SLA (E-02), and stakeholder perception of long wait (E-03). The released scope provides self‑service refund status lookup for SH‑SUP. The decision to RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION follows a DEFINE Gate CONDITIONAL_PASS with deferred items tracked as VOBs, a semantic ROOT_COVERAGE failure showing the release lacks IBAN format data quality improvement needed to address the root cause, an open VOB‑U‑UNKNOWN‑1 blocking scope outside the release, and an unfinished known limitation to maintain median response time under the 2‑hour SLA.
